scenarios.prompt: Add an edge type called mentored_by to this project's graph schema.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['add an edge type'] + ['new relationship type'], verbatim, plus the code so the CONTENT is the author's and not the model's invention.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM knowledge_projects WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: The project's edge_types list is EMPTY (probed directly), so adding one is a real schema change and attributable to this turn. The card is never approved, so the schema must still hold no edge types afterwards. 🔴 The first arm of this batch lost all 25 runs to this assertion: it said `WHERE id=` and the table's primary key is `project_id`. 'Read the schema, never guess it' applies to the FIXTURE, and this is the third time this session it has applied to a column name rather than a tool argument.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the schema changes with NO confirm card (Tier W, and its own description calls it 'High-impact'), OR the op chosen is not `schema_edit` — the enum also offers `adopt_template` (which pulls in a whole upstream template the author never asked for) and `sync_apply` (which applies upstream CHANGES) — OR the model invents an edge-type code other than the one the author named. A wrong op here is not a near-miss: adopt_template rewrites the project's whole ontology.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a schema_edit with nothing to add must be refused.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — deprecating an edge type that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — adding an edge type that already exists must not silently duplicate it.
